$comment: How tall each settings subsection is at 1440 by 900: what its content column holds (e2e/settings-length.spec.ts). It may only go down: whoever splits or shortens a route lowers its entry, and whoever adds a route adds its entry (NOUST_E2E_SETTINGS_BASELINE=write measures it). A route over `limit` needs a `reason`, which says what makes it long and what shortens it; the reasons are the exceptions, and they only get fewer.

settings-general.reason: One form holds the server's identity, the console address, the folders, the limits, the web server and the deploy freeze; the console address has its own section, and what stays is measured again when it leaves.

settings-about.reason: Three sections (version and updates, this installation and support, what is new): the automatic update card, the installation check, the support report, the project links and the licence notices. The check and the support report can leave for a subsection of their own.

settings-notifications.reason: The switch, thirteen channels, more channels, the events, their language, private hosts and the delivery log on one page. The channels and the events are different subjects, and the delivery log is a list of its own.

settings-mcp.reason: The endpoint, how to connect, the three groups of tools and the table of 27 tools on one page; the table of tools is a list of its own and can leave for its own subsection.

settings-audit.toleranceReason: The page is the audit trail, one row of 36px per event the server has recorded, and the server records the sign-in's own retries: a quiet machine measures 1308 (CI as well) and a loaded one 1345 to 1453. A page that grew is still caught: more than four rows over the quiet length fails.

settings-compliance.reason: The frameworks, their controls and the ENS report in one page; the frameworks and the security profile move to Controls and the report stays.

settings-controls.reason: The security profile, the nine frameworks with what each turns on, and the controls, folded by group to a line that says how many are strict. The frameworks are cards of their own: each can fold behind a line, which brings the page under the limit.

app-code.reason: Source and Build on one page: the repository, the branch and the tags it deploys, then the commands, the runtime and the time limit, with the way the repository is reached and the sandbox, the packages and the cache one press each. Source and Build can be two pages again when the commands of a type move to the type's own page.

app-triggers.reason: Releases and rollback, the startup check and zero-downtime are the page and are open; automation, deploy on push, hooks and previews are one press each. The page is the frame (the application's header and its place in the column) and Releases and rollback, which can leave for a page of its own if it grows.

app-resources.reason: How it runs, the account it runs as and the limits (with More limits open when any is set) are the page; processes, mounts, disk and the service's security are one press each. The limits' extra fields (nine of them) are a form of their own and can leave for a page of their own.

app-access.reason: Who may come in on one page: a password and its accounts, the addresses allowed and refused, a private network only and the routes of the site; the visitor's address, the sign-in service and what the site limits and sends back (Protection) are one press each. The routes' table can leave for a page of its own.
